requirement_set.title: Climate & Energy — GRI 302 and GRI 305 (2016 editions)
requirement_set.description: A focused subset of GRI energy and greenhouse gas disclosures for organizations that have identified climate change and energy as material topics. Designed for disclosure-readiness reviews of mid-sized companies.
requirement_set.effective_rule: Use for reports published before 1 January 2027. GRI 305 disclosures 305-1 to 305-5 are withdrawn when GRI 102: Climate Change 2025 takes effect, and GRI 302 is replaced by GRI 103: Energy 2025, both on 1 January 2027 (GRI, June 2025).

changes: 305-1: added element for biogenic CO2 emissions reported separately (305-1-c), previously omitted.

305-2: added conditional element for the market-based Scope 2 figure (305-2-b). It applies when the documents mention contractual instruments such as guarantees of origin, renewable energy certificates or power purchase agreements.
Initial curated subset covering GRI 302-1, 302-3, 302-4, 305-1 to 305-5 and GRI 2-5.

requirement_set.notes: Absence of evidence in the uploaded documents is not evidence of non-compliance. Applicability depends on the organization's material topics (GRI 3-3); reviewers can mark individual requirements as not applicable with a rationale.

evidence.text: Greenhouse gas emissions (tCO2e) — Scope 1 emissions (tCO2e): FY2024/25: 41,870; FY2023/24: 43,050

We report greenhouse gas emissions using the financial control approach, in line with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard. Emission factors are taken from DESNZ (2024) and global warming potentials from the IPCC Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). The inventory covers CO2, CH4, N2O and HFCs.
Our base year is FY2019/20. Base-year emissions are recalculated for structural changes above 5%.
Biogenic CO2 emissions from the use of biomass fuels were 1,240 tCO2e in FY2024/25 and are reported outside the scopes.
